step1_summary: Symptoms: Dry cough, runny nose, muscle aches, occasional headache, chills; symptoms started around 5 days ago; no shortness of breath or chest wheeze
Past medical history: Diabetes (5-6 years), Hypertension
Medications/allergies: Metformin, Lisinopril, occasional Paracetamol for current symptoms
Vital signs/exam findings: Mild redness at the back of the throat, no enlarged tonsils, no palpable neck glands, normal blood pressure reported

I: Viral Upper Respiratory Infection (Common Cold): Symptoms like dry cough, runny nose, and mild throat redness with no severe respiratory complications suggest a viral etiology.
E: Diabetes-related Immunosuppression: Though well-controlled, diabetes can predispose to infections which could influence symptom severity.

Mild throat redness with no severe respiratory symptoms (e.g., shortness of breath, wheezing)
opposing_evidence: None significant; symptoms align well with a typical viral infection
